outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: Cybersecurity and AI-driven enterprise software, led by Zscaler, CrowdStrike, and ServiceNow
strongest.reason: cybersecurity ETFs are up roughly 30% over the past year versus a loss for broader software ETFs, weekly security incidents hit a record high, and a recent survey found 0% of IT leaders see cybersecurity as a budget-cut candidate even as AI reallocation sweeps through other enterprise IT spending

strongest.area: Logic-side AI chips, led by Nvidia, Taiwan Semiconductor, and the broader chip-design software names (Cadence, Synopsys)
strongest.reason: these names are holding up notably better than memory and storage peers during the sector's month-long pullback, suggesting the AI-chip selloff is concentrated rather than sector-wide

weakest.area: Memory and storage semiconductors, particularly Micron
weakest.reason: memory names have led the broader chip-sector selloff over the past month on oversupply and profit-taking concerns, even as logic-chip peers have started to stabilize

weakest.area: Oracle within the AI infrastructure group
weakest.reason: it continues to lag its mega-cap cloud peers (Microsoft, Amazon, Google) despite its Google Cloud AI partnership, and coverage has specifically flagged this underperformance gap over the past week

outlook.nextStep: The growing split within semiconductors — logic and chip-design software holding up while memory names lag — is worth a closer look heading into the next earnings cycle, as is cybersecurity's continued decoupling from broader enterprise software. The Fed's September rate decision and the still-unresolved Intuitive Surgical competitive story are more event-driven and are probably better watched for confirmation than acted on now.

signals.title: Markets now pricing roughly 75% odds of a September rate cut
signals.body: Following the Fed's July 29 hold (with three regional presidents dissenting in favor of a hike), CME FedWatch data shows markets now assign around a 75% probability to a 25bp cut at the September 15-16 meeting. That's a meaningful shift from the split, hawkish-leaning tone of the July meeting itself, and leaves room for volatility if incoming inflation or labor data changes the calculus.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at how durable this rate-cut pricing is heading into the next inflation print

signals.title: Chip selloff is increasingly a memory-versus-logic story, not sector-wide
signals.body: Over the past month the semiconductor complex has been rough (SMH down roughly 9.5%), with memory and storage names like Micron and SK Hynix down more than 8% and Sandisk off 13% on oversupply and profit-taking concerns. But logic-side names have diverged: Nvidia, Taiwan Semiconductor, and Arm have each found buyers on recent down days, suggesting the pressure is concentrated in memory rather than spread evenly across chips.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether memory names catch up to the logic-chip stabilization or keep lagging

signals.title: Oracle's underperformance gap versus cloud peers keeps drawing coverage
signals.body: Despite reaffirmed hyperscaler capex commitments of $660-690 billion for 2026 and Oracle's own Google Cloud AI partnership, financial media has specifically called out Oracle's stock as lagging Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet over the past week, even as the broader AI-infrastructure capex narrative stays intact for the group.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether this is a temporary gap or a more structural re-rating

signals.title: Tesla's enterprise value increasingly tied to the Optimus bet
signals.body: Coverage of Tesla's latest strategic messaging suggests a growing share of the company's bull-case valuation now hinges on the Optimus humanoid-robot program rather than the core auto business, while Hong Kong- and China-listed humanoid names like UBTECH continue riding a broader regional robotics rally. Separately, Intuitive Surgical bounced back modestly after its sharp J&J-Ottava-driven slide, though the competitive overhang hasn't fully cleared.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at how much of Tesla's current valuation the market is now attributing to Optimus specifically

signals.title: Palantir holds its surge as BofA sets a $255 price target
signals.body: Palantir is holding on to most of its post-earnings gain after Bank of America set a $255 price target following the company's 93% year-on-year revenue growth, while ServiceNow continues to benefit from crossing $1 billion in AI annual contract value for the first time. Salesforce and Adobe are also participating in the broader enterprise-software rebound.
signals.focus: worth a closer look at whether analyst price-target revisions keep pace with the size of the recent moves

signals.title: Bitcoin holds near $65k as regulatory pipeline moves slowly in the background
signals.body: Bitcoin is trading in the $65,000-65,300 range, treated increasingly as a maturing institutional asset class even as several regulatory threads remain unresolved: CFTC guidance on cryptoasset perpetual futures continues to develop, and a comment period on proposed GENIUS Act stablecoin anti-money-laundering rules has closed with no final rule yet.
signals.focus: lower conviction right now on any near-term regulatory catalyst moving prices sharply either direction

signals.title: Cybersecurity's decoupling from broader software keeps strengthening on the data
signals.body: Average weekly security incidents per organization hit a record 2,270 in June, up 17% year-over-year, reinforcing why a recent survey found 0% of IT leaders view cybersecurity as a budget-cut candidate even as AI-driven reallocation sweeps through other enterprise IT categories. Cybersecurity-focused ETFs are up roughly 30% over the past year versus a loss for broader software ETFs over the same period.
signals.focus: worth a closer look given the budget-insulation story looks increasingly structural rather than one-quarter noise
